detail.longDescription:
I spent a lot of this year watching first a pair of squirrels, and now the next generation out back.  I'd been calling the original pair "Assle" & "Hassle" though I couldn't tell them apart and so the names were interchangeable.

This has me thinking about a possible fun project that I'll never get to: A small model trained to compare two images of furry critters and predict whether they are the same or different individuals.  Train on a wide enough range of mammals that it would hopefully generalize.  Then it could be run on a small camera device that could predict which critter of a number of named individuals it's pointed at.

That would be very useful - if it worked well enough - for watching the behavior of a group of animals that are hard for the human eye to tell apart without any kind of tagging/marking.

And it would be fun to see if it's an easy problem that a small local model that could run on a portable device of some kind could handle well.

#machinelearning #wildlife
